summary: Revise at 5.6 (Caiman 7, ship bar 7.5). There is an automatic revise before the art is even weighed: the template gate is red (verification.json has template_gate_passed false, with a template of 1,340,180 B against the 300,000 B procedural budget). verification.json is also stale. It dates from 18:10 while the build dates from 19:21, and its 1,231,390 triangles and 1,503,899 design bytes do not match report.json's 1,227,816 and 1,349,042. Every gate recorded in report.json is green. On the art: the rethink has landed well enough that the crown leaf now names itself as ivy at 300 px. It is the classic stylised three-lobed ivy glyph, with a long terminal lobe running along the band, rounded ears, a clinging stem and three black berries. But the ring is a plain polished D band with a handful of things on it, not ivy strangling a host. More than half of the visible outer surface in hero.png and face.png is bare polished metal. The density is far below Caiman's and nowhere near the Reptilia sheet. The modelling is CAD-flat in places. The terminal lobe of the crown leaf has no veins and melts into the band as a long smeared highlight, while its other edges are hard extruded ledges. The six small leaves are flat slabs with vertical walls, and in side.png and reverse.png they hang off the band edge as rectangular tabs. The rootlets read as a sawtooth of outward spikes, which says thorn or bramble (Rubus), not ivy. The berry collets are still deep cups, the reference-spinel mesh shows stair-stepped reflections in stones.png, and the peduncle on the right shoulder reads as a mechanical pin and bracket.
strengths: The crown leaf finally reads as ivy at 300 px: a long terminal lobe along the band axis, two short laterals, rounded basal ears and a petiole notch, with palmate veins from the base (hero-300, face-300).
The stem is a convincing round cable that hugs the band and carries the leaf's petiole, so one plant runs from the crown to the palm.
Black spinel cabochons are the right fruit colour, and the three berries are better bunched than in read tests 4 and 5.
The theme is consistent from face to palm: the same ivy leaf outline repeats on the shoulder and palm leaves (palm.png, reverse.png).
Every gate in report.json is green, with real margin on the body walls (0.815 mm minimum sampled against the 0.8 mm floor; field thinnest 1.89 mm).

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Ivy only: one stem, seven leaves of one outline family, three black berries. Nothing foreign. The leaves are sparse and evenly spotted round the palm, not crowded on a strangling stem, but they are one theme.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: Marginal pass. In hero-300 and face-300 the crown leaf is the stylised ivy glyph. The risk is the rootlet spikes, which read as thorns at 300 px and pull toward bramble. Fixing them (punch 3) makes this robust.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: In crown-close.png and face.png, the crown leaf's terminal lobe has no outline on its far half: it melts into the band as a long smeared highlight that ends in a faint chevron ledge, while the basal lobes have hard vertical walls. The vein cuts stop at the base. The cabochon reflections are stair-stepped (stones.png, all three berries), which is a tessellation artefact of reference-spinel.stl.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit
checklist.reason: Three black spinels in made collets, a correct ivy-berry colour, visible from the hero and the face. But the collets are still deep, straight-walled cups, so in stones.png the gold walls read as tubes, and three berries is a thin umbel. Punch 4.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The six small leaves are flat slabs of constant thickness with vertical walls. In side.png (lower left and bottom) and reverse.png (bottom) they stick off the band edge as rectangular tabs. The berry peduncle and stalk junction on the right shoulder (shoulder.png right of the berries; face.png far right) reads as a pin with a ball knob. The crown leaf's blade is flat, not cupped, with no lifted margins.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable. Procedural D-shape host, by design. The host's form is clean and unmarked.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: This is the only Vepres ring rendered so far. A slim D band with a single flat leaf is distinct from the planned canes, signets and roses, but it is also the weakest silhouette in the plan: in side.png it is almost a plain circle.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: There is one large form (the crown leaf), medium forms (the six small leaves, the berries) and small forms (rootlets, vein cuts). But by area the ring is mostly bare polished band: in hero.png, face.png and bare-vs-finished.png well over half of the visible outer surface is untouched host. Caiman and the Reptilia sheet are worked edge to edge. There is no bark on the stem, the leaves have no surface beyond three to five cuts, and the stem crosses the crown only once.

gates.verified: report.json geometry: watertight true, degenerate_faces 0, self_crossings 0; draft-gates.json matches
bore vertices_inside 0, nearest 9.30 mm at radius 9.3

gates.gate: Lost wax verdict Castable, thinnest wall >= 0.8 mm
gates.verified: field verdict Castable, thinnest_wall_mm 1.889; ray_walls body parts min 0.815 mm, 0 below the floor. Collets (0.247 mm) and rootlets (0.212 mm) are held at the 0.15 mm detail floor under Logan's 2026-10-03 rule for this ring

gates.gate: Sand field, ray release and clamp gates
gates.verified: draft.process LostWax, sand null; replaced by the 0.8 mm wall gate above

gates.gate: Stone count equals the preview, no metal in stones

gates.verified: report cold_reload_identical true; verification.json vertices_faces_normals_identical true (but see the stale-file note)
report gate 'casting pattern watertight, 0 degenerates, 0 crossings' true

gates.gate: Template gate: <= 4 design.set patches within the class budget
gates.verified: verification.json template_gate_passed false: 1 design.set patch (/manufacturing) is fine, but template_bytes 1,340,180 against size_budget_bytes 300,000 (procedural), size_review_required true. The file is also stale: 18:10 against the 19:21 build, and its triangles and design bytes do not match report.json

punch_list.change: Bring the template within the 300 KB procedural budget. Emit the leaf outlines, rootlet sets and stem path from script nodes instead of baked point lists, as the ring's Template plan (about 150 KB) intended. Then rerun --verify on the final build so verification.json is regenerated from the same design as report.json.
punch_list.acceptance: verification.json is newer than report.json, has template_gate_passed true, template_bytes <= 300,000 and design_set_patches <= 4, and its triangles equal report.json's export count.

punch_list.zone: Crown leaf, hub theta 110, blade theta about 70 to 115
punch_list.change: Sculpt the hero leaf. Carry the midrib and the two main lateral veins to their lobe tips as raised ribs 0.12 to 0.15 mm high, with a recessed vein web between them, not three short cuts at the base. Give the terminal lobe a true outline: the same 0.45 mm edge wall as the basal lobes, ending in a defined point, not a smeared fade. Cup the blade 0.3 mm and lift the margins and lobe tips 0.3 to 0.5 mm off the band, so the leaf has form, not a constant thickness.
punch_list.acceptance: In crown-close.png and face.png, the leaf's whole perimeter is a crisp continuous edge, including the terminal tip. Veins run to all three lobe tips. Shading across the blade shows a cupped surface with lifted tips. No long smeared highlight runs from the leaf into the band.

punch_list.zone: Rootlets along the stem, sets 1 and 2 (theta about 120 to 240, both flanks)
punch_list.change: Replace the outward sawtooth spikes with ivy aerial rootlets. Use short tufts of 3 to 5 fine filaments, 0.15 to 0.25 mm high, splayed down and outward onto the band surface from the stem's underside, in clusters every 1.2 to 1.5 mm. No single cones pointing away from the stem.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png and hero-300.png, the stem edge shows a fuzzy, gripping fringe pressed onto the band, not a row of teeth. A cold read of hero-300 says nothing about thorns or brambles.

punch_list.zone: Host coverage, all theta, crown and shoulders
punch_list.change: Make the ivy strangle the band. Run the stem a second pass across the crown, or add a second stem crossing the first, so stem covers the crown twice as the original concept intended. Add 4 to 6 more leaves in three sizes (2.5, 3.5 and 5 mm), overlapping each other and the stem on the shoulders, with petioles visible. Put fine bark (longitudinal striation, 0.05 to 0.08 mm, side-face or stem-only as the doctrine allows) on the stem.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png and face.png, bare polished host is at most 35% of the visible outer surface (it is over 60% now). In side.png the outline is broken by leaves and stem on at least six places round the circle.

punch_list.zone: Small leaves: Left shoulder, Shoulder, Palm, Low west, Low palm, Low east
punch_list.change: Stop the flat slabs. Each leaf must conform to the band's curvature, with rounded or drafted edges (fillet at least 0.15 mm, no vertical walls) and a midrib plus two veins. Where a leaf meets the band edge, curl it over the edge onto the side face (the planned edge-leaf loft), not out into space as a flat tab.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and reverse.png, no leaf shows a rectangular straight-walled tab beyond the band's edge. In palm.png, every small leaf has visible veins and rounded edges.

punch_list.zone: Berry umbel: Berry 1 to 3, collets, stalks, peduncle (right shoulder, theta about 30 to 60)
punch_list.change: Grow the umbel to 5 berries, the third and fourth smaller (2.2 mm), on visible stalks from one peduncle point. Thin the collet walls to 0.25 mm and drop the collet top so at least 60% of each cabochon's height stands proud. Merge the peduncle into the stem with a blended swelling, and remove the pin-and-knob look at its junction. Re-tessellate reference-spinel.stl (at least 128 segments round and 64 rows) so the berries render smooth.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png, each berry's black area is at least twice its visible gold rim, and the reflections are smooth gradients with no pixel stair-steps. In shoulder.png, the peduncle reads as a stalk, not a bracket. In hero-300, the cluster reads as a bunch of berries.
